title: The cartridge and how it fires
subtitle: Bullet, case, powder and primer

lines: In this episode, we look inside the cartridge, and at how it fires.
The aim is for you to understand how a cartridge works, and to identify the correct ammunition for your firearm.

scenes.heading: Not just bullets
bullets: The bullet is only one component
Four components: bullet, case, powder, primer
Cartridge: civilian term. Round: military term

lines.text: Ammunition is often incorrectly referred to as bullets.
But the bullet is only one component of a complete cartridge.
The complete cartridge has four basic components: the bullet, the case, the powder, or propellant, and the primer.
This complete assembly is known as a cartridge, the civilian term, or a round, the military term.

lines: Either term is correct.

lines.text: Here is a cartridge in cross section.
At the front is the bullet.
Inside the case is the powder.
And at the base is the primer.
The book's cross section of a case also names the primer pocket and the flash hole.

scenes.definition: A small metal cup containing an explosive compound. Both heat sensitive and pressure sensitive.
lines: The primer is a small metal cup containing an explosive compound.
The primer is both heat sensitive and pressure sensitive.
When the primer is struck by the firing pin, a small explosion occurs to ignite the powder.
This explosion is referred to as a flash, as it is this flash that will ignite the powder.

scenes.definition: Burns, creating expanding gasses. Modern ammunition uses Nitro Cellulose powder, a smokeless powder.
lines: The powder burns, creating expanding gasses.
These expanding gasses create a pressure build-up, which will push the bullet down the barrel and out towards the target.
In modern day ammunition, Nitro Cellulose powder is used.
It is a smokeless powder.

scenes.definition: A brass, steel or copper cylinder closed at one end. It holds all the other components together.
lines: The case is a brass, steel or copper cylinder, closed at one end.
Its function is to hold all the other components together.
It is the only component that can be re-used, or reloaded.

scenes.definition: Usually lead covered with a copper jacket. The only component that leaves the barrel and strikes the target.
lines: The bullet is usually made of lead, covered with a copper jacket.
The bullet is the only component that leaves the barrel and strikes the target.

lines.text: Now let's follow the cartridge firing sequence, inside the firearm.
Squeezing the trigger on the firearm will cause the firing pin to strike the primer.
The primer explodes, sending a flash, or flame, into the case.
The powder burns, creating a pressure build-up behind the bullet.
This pressure build-up will push the bullet down the barrel and out towards the target.

scenes.heading: The firing sequence
bullets: Primer explodes: a flash into the case
Powder burns: pressure behind the bullet
Bullet pushed down the barrel, towards the target
lines: Once more, in order: the trigger is squeezed, and the firing pin strikes the primer.
The primer explodes, and sends a flash into the case.
The flame ignites the powder.
The powder burns, and pressure builds up behind the bullet.
And that pressure pushes the bullet down the barrel and out towards the target.

scenes.question: Which is the only component of the cartridge that strikes the target?
lines: Which is the only component of the cartridge that strikes the target?
Pause the video if you need a moment.
reveal: The book says the bullet is the only component that leaves the barrel and strikes the target.

scenes.question: Which component is the only one that can be re-used?
lines: And which component is the only one that can be re-used?
reveal: It is the only component that can be re-used, or reloaded.

points: Four components: bullet, case, powder, primer
Powder burns; gas pressure pushes the bullet
The case holds it together, and can be reloaded
Only the bullet strikes the target
lines: So, a cartridge has four components: bullet, case, powder and primer.
The primer is heat and pressure sensitive, and its flash ignites the powder.
The powder burns, and the pressure pushes the bullet down the barrel.
The case holds everything together, and can be reloaded.
And only the bullet strikes the target.
